01 / CASE STUDY
APPLIED AI / FORECASTING / DECISION SUPPORT
TGSRTC Public Transport Demand Platform
WINNING SOLUTION
Winner — Telangana AI Rising / AI4TG Grand Challenge

Challenge: Optimizing Public Transport Utilization with AI. Innodatatics was publicly recognized as the winning team for this transport use case.

TEAM CONTEXT

The solution was developed by the Innodatatics team during my internship as its entry for the TGSRTC public-transport challenge. The recognition belongs to the team.

PROBLEM

The challenge explored how AI-driven forecasting could help people understand and optimize public transport utilization for TGSRTC.

MY CONTRIBUTION

As part of the winning team, I contributed substantially to the web application used to surface and communicate the forecasting results. I focused on turning forecast outputs and related insights into an interface stakeholders could explore and understand.

Implementation

My work centered on the application and presentation layer: structuring forecast outputs so they could be inspected, compared, and communicated clearly through the web experience.

Outcome and lesson

The team solution was selected as the winning entry in its challenge category. The project reinforced that a forecast becomes useful when people can interpret it through a clear, dependable interface.

PUBLIC RECORD
The recognition, in its original context.

These posts document the team, the challenge, and the winning solution. They are included here as external evidence alongside the technical case study.

02 / CASE STUDY
GENAI / RETRIEVAL
Conversational RAG Application
CONTEXT

Document-grounded assistants need retrieval and conversation state to cooperate across multiple turns.

PROBLEM

Preserve conversational context while retrieving relevant chunks and keeping generated answers connected to source material.

ROLE

Implemented the application flow using Streamlit, LangGraph state, Hugging Face embeddings, retrieval, and Groq inference.

PRODUCT VIEW
Grounded answers, visible sources.

A visual interpretation of the verified retrieval flow: question, sources, grounded answer, and conversation state in one inspectable interface.

Implementation

LangGraph holds the conversational state. The retriever uses Hugging Face embeddings to select document chunks, and Groq inference generates a response from that context.

Outcome and lesson

The result is a multi-turn retrieval application whose architecture makes state, retrieval, and generation explicit. Future work would expand evaluation around retrieval quality, source coverage, and failure handling.

03 / CASE STUDY
VISION / RETRIEVAL
Computer Vision Image Search
CONTEXT

Large image collections are difficult to search when their useful information exists only inside the pixels.

PROBLEM

Detect visual objects, convert detections into searchable metadata, and return relevant images through a simple interface.

ROLE

Built the detection, indexing, query, and Streamlit presentation workflow described here.

VISUAL EVIDENCE / SEARCH PIPELINE
From pixels to an inspectable index.

Three compact records show the source context, the object collection, and the detection metadata that supports visual retrieval.

Implementation

YOLOv11 detects objects in source images. Detection labels become an index that a query can match before the interface presents relevant images.

Outcome and lesson

The verified result is a visual-search workflow connecting detection to retrieval. The limitations are tied to detector coverage, ambiguous labels, and the need for stronger ranking when many images share the same object class.

What each artifact actually proves.

Lesson: Simple labels hide ambiguity, so examples and failure cases matter as much as the prediction itself.

Six builds. Four public codebases.

The public repositories open the implementation behind ZAP, LOOP, Driver Drowsiness, and Creditworthy Borrower. Each entry also names the concrete stack, build focus, contribution, and lesson.

The Sentiment Classifier and Voice-to-Order Agent remain private prototypes, so they are presented through their verified project material rather than linked to unrelated repositories.
